[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Alternating Subsequence** [CF 1343C · Alternating Subsequence](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1343/C){rating="1200"}

"Maximum length first" decides the shape for you: signs split the array into maximal *same-sign runs*, and any alternating subsequence can take at most one element from each run (two from one run would sit adjacent with the same sign somewhere in between). Taking exactly one per run is the unique way to reach maximum length — so the only freedom left is *which* element of each run, and to maximise the sum you simply take the run's **maximum** (largest positive, or smallest-in-absolute-value negative, i.e. `max` either way). That is the group pointer of @sec-tp-runs/@sec-tp-p6-a with the chain test changed from "next value $= + 1$" to "next sign $=$ same".

[Solved in full in @sec-tp-p6-b.]{.card-link}
